US hospital price transparency

Who actually publishes their prices?

Hospitals must publish their prices in a downloadable file and link to it from /cms-hpt.txt. Every hospital in the CMS list was checked: total.

Method

How a hospital gets its label

1. Find the website

Use the website in the CMS list. If none works, mark the hospital not assessed.

2. Fetch the pointer

Check /cms-hpt.txt and /.well-known/cms-hpt.txt. If the site refuses the request, mark it blocked.

3. Match the facility

Match the hospital to the right entry. For unclear names, compare the name and address.

4. Read the file

Open the charge file and read its version and update date.

Limits

What these results mean

The tracker checks whether files exist and open. Prices and fields inside them are not fully verified.

Results can go stale

Every label is tied to the snapshot date. A hospital may have changed its files since then.

“File located” describes discovery

It means a file was found and opened. The check does not cover every price, code, or required field.

“Issue observed” needs verification

A discovery, request, date, or template check raised a concern. It may reflect a hospital issue, a changed URL, or a limitation of our tools.

Blocked is not a verdict

The website refused the request. These hospitals are excluded from the compliance rate.

Not assessed means no result

Domain, access, or hospital identity remains unresolved. A working website or file may exist. These hospitals are excluded from every rate.

Matching is automated, and imperfect

Software matches hospital names to file entries. Some matches may be wrong or missing.

The registry underneath has its own lag

Hospital names and websites come from CMS. That list can lag behind closures, mergers, and rebrands.

File age is only as honest as the file

The date comes from the file's declared metadata. We do not substitute the website's deployment date, and the declaration itself may be wrong.

This does not predict patient charges

These files do not show what a patient will pay. Use the hospital's estimator or billing office.

Corrections are welcome and remain local

A correction changes only your browser. It does not change the published results.

Record an update

“Open in mail app” hands the draft to the device's default mail client through a mailto: link. Nothing is sent from this page; send it from the mail app, then save it to the log.

Found a domain or file outside the crawl? Record it here. Corrections remain separate from the crawl and are always identified as manual; the audit figures on this page do not move.
